plain_english_policy: This bill prohibits businesses, property owners, and employers in Alabama from creating policies that ban employees or visitors from transporting or storing firearms/ammunition in their personal vehicles, provided the person is legally allowed to possess them. It allows civil lawsuits for damages (including attorney fees) if a business enforces such bans, reinstates fired workers with benefits/seniority rights, and limits liability for businesses regarding injuries caused by others' actions involving those firearms.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would shift policy to protect an individual's right to carry/transport legally owned guns in their car at private or public establishments (e.g., stores, restaurants), reversing potential bans. It creates a legal framework where businesses cannot restrict this activity and must face civil penalties if they do.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Ford (Commerce & Small Business) sponsored the bill to advance protections for lawful gun carriers in vehicles.
evidence_quotes: This bill would prohibit a business entity... from establishing policies against persons transporting or storing a firearm or ammunition when the person is otherwise in compliance with all other applicable laws under certain conditions.
A person who is injured or incurs damages, or the survivors of a person killed, as a result of a violation of subsection (b) may file a civil action...
An employee discharged... for a violation of a policy or rule prohibited by subsection (b) is entitled to full recovery...
No business entity... shall be held liable in any civil action for damages, injuries, or death resulting from or arising out of another person's actions involving a firearm...
